Reference.title: Windows Security Event 4732 (member added to security-enabled local group)

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A Windows account or group change was audited (account create/enable/disable/delete, password reset, account modification, or group-membership add/remove) and reached the SOC because the rule deliberately EXCLUDES the known administration path — it drops changes originating from 192.168.166.1 (the admin jump host) and machine-account activity (related.user ending in "$"). So what remains is human-driven account change from a NON-standard source, which is exactly the population worth reviewing. The triage question: is this authorised identity administration performed off the normal path, or an attacker manipulating accounts for persistence or privilege?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Account and group changes are the levers of persistence and privilege on the INTDOM domain — a backdoor account, a re-enabled dormant account, a password reset on a service account, or an add to a privileged group all grant durable access to banking systems. Changes made off the sanctioned administration path are the ones most likely to be unauthorised.

Assets.AssetType: Windows member servers and workstations where accounts/groups are managed

LogSources.LogSource: Windows Security event log — logs-system.security-* (verified live: 4720/4722/4724/4725/4726/4738/4740/4732 etc. present; SubjectUserName, TargetUserName, related.user, host.name populated)

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows "User Account Management" and "Security Group Management" auditing shipped via Elastic Agent to logs-system.security-* (verified live).

winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName (actor) and winlog.event_data.TargetUserName (affected account) populated on the change events (verified live). MemberName/MemberSid populate on group add/remove (4728/4729/4732/4733/4756/4757).

RULE SCOPE: the detection filters out source 192.168.166.1 (admin jump host) and machine accounts (related.user:*$). A change that legitimately comes from that jump host will NOT reach this alert — so an alert here means the change came from somewhere else, which is itself a triage signal.

Signal.Name: Account/group change off the admin path
Signal.Details: A 47xx account/group-management event for a real (non-machine) account, sourced from something other than the admin jump host. SubjectUserName is the actor; TargetUserName the affected account; host.name the DC/server.

Signal.Name: Actor burst
Signal.Details: One SubjectUserName performing many changes across distinct targets in a short window indicates mass account manipulation rather than a single administrative edit.

Input.name: $actor
Input.description: The user who performed the change (winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName from the alert).

Input.name: $target_user
Input.description: The account that was changed (winlog.event_data.TargetUserName from the alert).

ImmediateCapture.Item: Event code / operation from the alert (create, enable, disable, delete, pw-reset, group-add/remove) and the host.name

InitialAssessment.Rule: If $actor is a recognised IAM/helpdesk admin, only $target_user was affected, and the change maps to a ticket, lean authorised administration performed off the usual path (False Positive / authorised).

If $actor changed MANY accounts in the window (INV-02), the operation is a privilege grant (group-add), the target is a service/privileged account, or $actor is a normal user with no admin duty, escalate.

Investigation.Goal: Decide whether the account/group change to $target_user is authorised identity administration or attacker account-manipulation, and whether it is part of a broader burst by $actor.

Step.name: Reconstruct the change(s) to the target account
Step.Purpose: Confirm what happened to $target_user, who did it, on which host, and when — the anchor facts for the change-record comparison.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE winlog.event_data.TargetUserName == "$target_user" AND event.code IN ("4720","4722","4723","4724","4725","4726","4738","4740","4767","4728","4729","4732","4733","4756","4757") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL op = CASE(event.code=="4720","create",event.code=="4722","enable",event.code=="4723","pw-change",event.code=="4724","pw-reset",event.code=="4725","disable",event.code=="4726","delete",event.code=="4738","account-change",event.code=="4740","lockout",event.code=="4767","unlock",event.code=="4728","group-add-global",event.code=="4729","group-rem-global",event.code=="4732","group-add-local",event.code=="4733","group-rem-local",event.code=="4756","group-add-univ",event.code=="4757","group-rem-univ",event.code) | STATS events = COUNT(*), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp), actors = VALUES(winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName), dcs = VALUES(host.name) BY op | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 25
Step.AnalystNotes: A single change by a recognised admin identity is routine. Multiple actors touching one account, a group-add (privilege grant), or a create/enable of a previously-unknown account is the higher-risk case. Record first_seen/last_seen to align with the actor-burst window in INV-02.

Step.name: Profile the actor's account-management activity
Step.Purpose: Distinguish a one-off administrative edit from mass account manipulation: how many distinct accounts $actor created, enabled, disabled, deleted, reset, or re-grouped in the window.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName == "$actor" AND event.code IN ("4720","4722","4723","4724","4725","4726","4738","4740","4767","4728","4729","4732","4733","4756","4757") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL op = CASE(event.code IN ("4728","4732","4756"),"group-add",event.code IN ("4729","4733","4757"),"group-remove",event.code=="4720","create",event.code=="4722","enable",event.code=="4725","disable",event.code=="4726","delete",event.code=="4724","pw-reset",event.code=="4738","account-change",event.code) | STATS n = COUNT(*), targets = COUNT_DISTINCT(winlog.event_data.TargetUserName), sample_targets = VALUES(winlog.event_data.TargetUserName) BY op | SORT n DESC | LIMIT 25
Step.AnalystNotes: A single change with no other operations is consistent with routine administration. Many changes across many distinct targets = mass manipulation. Note especially create-then-group-add sequences (attacker provisioning a privileged backdoor) or many password resets (account takeover preparation).

Step.name: Establish where the actor is operating from
Step.Purpose: Because the rule excludes the admin jump host, the actor reached the DC/server from somewhere else — identify that origin to judge whether it is a legitimate admin workstation or an unexpected/compromised host.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE winlog.event_data.TargetUserName == "$actor" AND event.code IN ("4624","4625","4672") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL ev = CASE(event.code=="4624","logon-success",event.code=="4625","logon-fail",event.code=="4672","special-privs",event.code) | STATS n = COUNT(*), sources = VALUES(source.ip), hosts = VALUES(host.name), logon_types = VALUES(winlog.event_data.LogonType) BY ev | SORT n DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: Interactive/RDP logon from a recognised admin workstation aligns with authorised (if off-path) administration. Logon from an unexpected host, a workstation that should not administer AD, or a source with prior failed logons (4625) before the change points to a compromised identity making the change. 4672 (special privileges) confirms the session held admin rights.

Node.Condition: INV-02 shows $actor changed MANY distinct accounts in the window, OR INV-01 shows a create/enable of an unknown account or a privileged group-add, AND $actor is not an authorised administrator or acted outside a change window.
Node.Result: True Positive (Attacker account manipulation for persistence/privilege — escalate to IR)

Node.Condition: INV-03 shows $actor logged on from an unexpected/compromised host (or after failed logons) before making the change, and no ticket authorises it.
Node.Result: True Positive (Change made from a compromised identity/host — escalate to IR)

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows a single change by a recognised IAM/helpdesk admin, INV-02 shows no burst, INV-03 shows a legitimate admin workstation, and the change maps to an approved ticket.
Node.Result: False Positive (Authorised identity administration performed off the usual admin path)

Node.Condition: A provisioning/automation account performed the change per a known job whose scope matches INV-02 (e.g. scheduled group sync) but not via the excluded jump host.
Node.Result: Misconfiguration (Automation running off-path — correct routing/scope, do not blanket-exception)

Node.Condition: Actor authorisation or the business justification for the change cannot be established from IAM/CMDB/ticketing, or breadth is borderline.

FalsePositive.Definition: An authorised administrator or approved automation made the account/group change as part of documented identity administration — the authorising context (ticket, admin role, legitimate origin) must be shown, not inferred from the account name alone.

Indicators.Item: $actor is a known IAM/helpdesk/admin identity acting within its role (INV-01).
No actor burst (INV-02) and a legitimate admin workstation origin (INV-03).
Change maps to an approved ticket / documented lifecycle event.

SOCAction.Item: Verify the ticket and the actor's authorisation; close as false_positive.
If a legitimate admin routinely administers off the jump host, either route them onto the sanctioned path or scope an exception for that actor/source — do not disable the rule.

TruePositive.Definition: An adversary manipulated accounts/groups for persistence or privilege — creating a backdoor account, re-enabling a dormant one, resetting a service-account password, or adding to a privileged group.

Indicators.Item: Actor burst across distinct accounts, or create-then-group-add provisioning (INV-01/INV-02).
Change made from an unexpected/compromised host or after failed logons (INV-03).
Actor is a normal/non-admin account, or the target is a privileged/service account.

SOCAction.Item: Open an incident; treat $actor as potentially compromised; reverse unauthorised changes (remove backdoor account / group membership; force credential reset).
Reconstruct the actor's full recent activity (logons, privilege changes, data access); contain the source host.

Misconfiguration.Definition: An internal automation or admin script made account/group changes off the sanctioned path — operationally driven, not malicious.

Indicators.Item: A service/automation account performed the changes on a schedule from a non-jump-host system.
Breadth matches a known sync/provisioning job.

SOCAction.Item: Engage the automation owner to route it via the sanctioned path or correct its scope; document.
Track under identity hygiene; keep the rule enabled.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm scope from INV-02: one change or a burst? A burst is an active-incident trigger.
Verify $actor's authorisation and origin (INV-03) with IAM; if unauthorised or from a compromised host, disable $actor and revoke its sessions.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Reverse unauthorised changes (remove backdoor accounts / group memberships; reset affected credentials); reconstruct the actor's full activity timeline.
Contain the source host; hunt the same account-manipulation pattern across the estate.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Review who holds account/group-management rights and enforce administration only via the sanctioned jump host; tighten delegation to IAM roles.
Alert on off-path privileged-group adds and actor bursts as a higher-severity correlated analytic.

Escalation.Trigger: Actor-burst changes, create-then-group-add provisioning, a privileged/service-account target, change from a compromised host, or unverifiable actor authorisation.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Ticket and actor authorisation verified; origin confirmed as a legitimate admin workstation.
No actor burst; change consistent with documented identity administration.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Unauthorised changes reversed; $actor contained and full activity timeline reconstructed.
Source host contained; estate swept; evidence preserved; incident documented.
